name: lft
desc: Layer Four Traceroute (LFT), an advanced traceroute tool
why: Traceroute that sends TCP SYN probes to get past firewalls, a neat door into how routers and middleboxes actually answer packets.

brief.what_it_is: LFT (Layer Four Traceroute) is described in its Homebrew formula as an advanced traceroute tool. The formula installs two executables, lft and whob. The scout note says it sends TCP SYN probes so that traces can get past firewalls, but I could not read the project's own description to confirm this. I have no details on input or output formats.
brief.why_it_exists: I could not read the author's framing. The formula description only says it is an advanced traceroute tool.
brief.standout: The scout note says it uses TCP SYN probes instead of the usual ICMP or UDP probes, which can get traces through firewalls and show how routers and middleboxes respond to packets. This is unverified because the README was not readable.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://pwhois.org/lft/ returned HTTP 403, so I could not read the README or docs. I also tried https://github.com/synfin/lft, a guessed repository URL, and it returned HTTP 404. Everything here comes from the Homebrew formula metadata and the scout note, not from the project's documentation. Installation, platform support, licence and commands are all unknown.
fetch_log: https://github.com/synfin/lft - failed, HTTP 404 (guessed repository URL, not linked from the homepage, since the homepage could not be read)
